definitions.gloss: formal clothes, festive attire, best clothes
definitions.explanation: Special clothing worn for celebrations, ceremonies, and other important occasions. Traditionally refers to kimono or other Japanese-style formal garments, but can also refer to any dressy outfit.

examples.japanese: {晴|は}れ{着|ぎ}を{着|き}て{出|で}かけた。
examples.english: I dressed up and went out.

examples.japanese: {成人式|せいじんしき}に{晴|は}れ{着|ぎ}の{振袖|ふりそで}を{着|き}た。
examples.english: I wore a festive furisode kimono to the coming-of-age ceremony.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちが{七五三|しちごさん}の{晴|は}れ{着|ぎ}を{着|き}て、{神社|じんじゃ}にお{参|まい}りする{姿|すがた}は{微笑|ほほえ}ましい。
examples.english: The sight of children dressed in their festive attire visiting the shrine for Shichi-Go-San is heartwarming.

notes:
USAGE:
Derived from {晴|は}れ (hare), which refers to special, public, or ceremonial occasions in Japanese culture (as opposed to {褻|け}/ke, the everyday). Often refers to traditional Japanese formal wear such as {振袖|ふりそで}, {紋付|もんつき}{袴|はかま}, or other kimono. Also used more broadly for any best or dressy outfit.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {晴|は}れ{着|ぎ}を{着|き}る: to wear formal/festive clothes
- {晴|は}れ{着|ぎ}の{姿|すがた}: the sight of someone in formal attire
- {晴|は}れ{着|ぎ}{姿|すがた}: dressed in formal attire

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {正装|せいそう}: formal dress (general, not limited to Japanese style)
- {礼服|れいふく}: formal wear, ceremonial dress
